_comment: Donation methods. Validated at load by lib/donate.mjs — any method whose address fails its checksum is DROPPED and logged, because a wrong address loses every donation silently. ADDRESSES ARE NOT STORED HERE: each crypto method names an `addressEnv`, and the deployment supplies that environment variable. A receiving address is public once live, but committing it would bind it permanently to this repository and its history.
_setup: 1. Set the env var named by each method's `addressEnv` to YOUR receiving address (see .env.example). Addresses are deliberately NOT committed. 2. The file hot-reloads; no restart needed. 3. Watch the server log for which methods went live and which were dropped and why. 4. Send a tiny test transaction on each chain BEFORE announcing it — especially XMR and SOL, which are shape-checked only (see _shape_only_warning).
_shape_only_warning: XMR and SOL are shape-checked, NOT checksum-verified. Monero uses Keccak-256, which node:crypto does not provide. Solana addresses are raw Ed25519 public keys and carry no checksum at all — a typo that still decodes to 32 bytes is undetectable. A wrong address on either loses every donation sent to it. Test both.
_privacy_note: Privacy differs enormously between these. XMR hides sender, receiver and amount on-chain. BTC, LTC and SOL are fully transparent: every donation to those addresses is public forever and links donors to each other, and anyone can read the full history of this site's income. The `privacy` field is shown to donors so they choose knowingly rather than assuming a coin is private because it is on this list.
_why_these_six: ALL ARE CRYPTO: there is no card option, so a visitor without a wallet cannot donate at all — a deliberate choice, not an oversight. SOL and USDC are ONE address and one wallet (`DONATE_SOL_ADDRESS`), listed separately only because a donor holding dollars should not have to know that USDC is an SPL token on Solana. ETH is listed with an explicit push toward L2s: the same 0x address receives on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and Optimism, and mainnet gas frequently exceeds the size of a donation this site receives. A donor holding DOGE can still pay through the optional swap path, which settles to Monero.
heading: Support ZoFHub
blurb: ZoFHub is free, has no accounts, and never sells your data. Donations are voluntary, non-refundable, and buy nothing — no perks, no ad removal, no special access.

methods.label: Solana
methods.note: Cheapest and fastest here — fees are a fraction of a cent. This same address also receives USDC. Public ledger.

methods.label: USDC (on Solana)
methods.note: A dollar-pegged token, so the value does not swing. SOLANA NETWORK ONLY — USDC sent on Ethereum, Base, Polygon or any other chain to this address is lost permanently. Public ledger.

methods.label: Bitcoin
methods.note: Most widely held. On-chain fees can exceed a small donation — use Lightning for anything under about $20. Public ledger.

methods.label: Litecoin
methods.note: Cheap, fast, and on every exchange and PayPal. Public ledger.

methods.label: Ethereum
methods.note: Mainnet gas often costs more than a small donation — send on an L2 (Base, Arbitrum, Optimism) instead, where fees are cents. The SAME address works on all of them. Public ledger.

methods.label: Monero
methods.note: Private by default — sender, receiver and amount are all hidden. The only option here that is not a public ledger.
